card.title: Half-life and binding energy — the nuclear ledger

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Rutherford's scattering revealed the tiny dense nucleus (10⁻¹⁴ m in a 10⁻¹⁰ m atom). Assembled nucleons weigh LESS than their parts — the missing mass (defect) became binding energy via E = mc², peaking per nucleon at iron-56. Unstable nuclei decay exponentially with decay constant λ; half-life T½ = 0.693/λ is the statistical halving time. Fission splits heavy nuclei, fusion joins light ones — both climb toward iron, releasing the difference.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: E = mc² (1 u = 931.5 MeV)  ·  B.E. = Δm·c², curve peaks at Fe-56 (~8.8 MeV/nucleon)  ·  N = N₀e^(−λt), activity A = λN  ·  T½ = ln2/λ ≈ 0.693/λ  ·  T½ = 8 days → after 24 days (3 lives): (1/2)³ = 1/8 remains

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Exponential decay is statistical — exact for large N, meaningless for a few atoms. Binding-energy comparisons need per-NUCLEON values (totals mislead across masses). Fission needs a fissile seed + neutrons; stellar fusion needs million-kelvin confinement.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Pair production (γ → e⁻ + e⁺) and annihilation (e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ) convert mass ↔ energy directly, with 1.02 MeV threshold. Isotopes share chemistry (same Z) but differ in stability. Carbon-14 dating and medical tracers are half-life applications.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: T½ = 8 days, after 24 days = 3 half-lives → remaining fraction (1/2)³ = 1/8; activity falls by the same factor (A = λN) (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Mass defect variant: Δm between parts and nucleus × 931.5 MeV/u = binding energy — divide by A for the per-nucleon ranking.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Half-life predicts populations, never single atoms (quantum randomness). E = mc² prices conversion but says nothing about reaction RATES (tunnelling, cross-sections rule). The liquid-drop picture behind binding trends is semi-empirical — shell structure adds the fine print.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Decay: dN/dt = −λN (constant per-nucleus probability) → separate and integrate → N = N₀e^(−λt); set N = N₀/2 → T½ = ln2/λ. Binding: weigh parts (Z·mₚ + N·mₙ + electrons) minus atomic mass → Δm → ×c²; the Fe-56 maximum explains why fission AND fusion both release energy.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Half-life questions: count lives n = t/T½, remaining = (1/2)ⁿ. 'Define decay constant + T½ relation' is a 2-marker (NEB 2024). Binding: defect → ×931.5 → ÷A. Fission = split heavy, fusion = join light, both → toward iron.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (2): decay constant + half-life relation. NEB 2023 (3): mass defect vs binding energy. NEB 2023 (3): T½ = 8 days — fraction after 24 days + activity change.
